newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes lower after late liquidation.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes lower after late liquidation.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures succumbed to a lingering bearish sentiment on Thursday, reversing afternoon gains to end the session lower.
June Brent settled down 12 cents at $17.69 a barrel, having dipped to a low of $17.61 shortly before the close.
"We recovered from the initial (downside) move, but I think things got a bit jittery and we saw some selling come back later on," said one broker.
Earlier, Brent rallied to $17.95 after NYMEX products held key support levels and reversed opening losses.
Forecasts for cool temperatures in the key heating oil market of the U.S. Northeast was the main driver behind the gains, brokers said.
Private forecaster Weather Services Corp (WSC) said temperatures would run two to six degrees Fahrenheit below normal on Thursday, dipping to between six and 12 degrees below normal on Saturday.

Sun Co Inc, a major supplier of heating oil in the region, said on Thursday that the cold spell had already cleared out its stocks and it was unlikely to resume supplies to distributors until late next week.

But bearish U.S. inventory data, particularly for gasoline, continued to haunt traders, and both NYMEX heating oil and unleaded gasoline futures fell from highs pulling the rest of the complex with them.
U.S. stocks swelled unexpectedly last week, and the American Petroleum Institute (API) said on Wednesday that gasoline supply would meet peak demand this summer, even if it grew by 2.5 percent.
Earlier, May gas oil ended its session 50 cents down at $162.25 a tonne, off a low of $161.75.
